articles.title: Bill Oddie Reflects on Rochdale Roots in BBC Documentary
articles.excerpt: Bill Oddie, the renowned television personality, explored his Rochdale heritage in a recent episode of Who Do You Think You Are?, revealing personal family history and insights into his childhood.
articles.content_html:
Bill Oddie, the television personality known for his work on The Goodies and Springwatch, explored his roots in Rochdale during a recent episode of the BBC show Who Do You Think You Are?. Oddie, who was born at Birch Hill Hospital in Littleborough in 1941, moved away from the area at the age of seven when his father took a job in Birmingham.

In the episode, Oddie discovered that his ancestors were all mill workers, including his grandmother Emily Worrall, who was born in Rochdale and likely worked at Arrow Mill in Castleton from the age of 13. He reflected on his childhood relationship with his mother, Lilian, who was committed to a psychiatric institution when he was young. Oddie believed she suffered from schizophrenia and had abandoned him, only seeing her a few times before her death in 1990.

During filming, he met two nurses who cared for his mother, who informed him that she was actually a 'manic depressive'. Oddie also learned about the loss of a sister, Margaret, who died shortly after birth due to a tragic incident involving their grandmother. This new understanding prompted Oddie to reassess his feelings towards his mother, expressing regret for his previous harsh judgments.

Oddie's journey into his family history has been described as transformative, allowing him to gain insight into the challenges his mother faced and fostering a sense of empathy for her struggles. He stated, "This journey has been a real lifesaver... I wish I'd known her better and I wish she'd known me."
